title: Mid-Year Formulary Change Terms: Notice, Grandfathering and Positive Changes
content:
For each formulary of the Formulary Benefit, these terms govern changes made to the drug list during the plan year: the advance notice owed to affected members before a negative change, whether current users are grandfathered, the claim lookback that defines a current user, and when positive changes take effect.

| Term | Exclusive | Value | Standard | Preferred Drug List | Broad | Open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Advance notice before a negative change takes effect (calendar days) | 30 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 90 |
| Current users keep the prior status through plan year end | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Paid-claim lookback before the change effective date that makes a member a current user (calendar days) | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 |
| Positive changes take effect on P&T approval without notice | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

The columns are the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary, Northbridge Value Formulary, Northbridge Standard Formulary, Northbridge Preferred Drug List, Northbridge Broad Formulary and Northbridge Open Formulary.

## Definitions used in this table

- A **negative change** is a drug moved to NF, excluded, or raised to a higher tier.
- A **positive change** is a lower tier or a newly added drug.
- The **advance notice** is the number of calendar days by which the notice must come before the change effective date.

*Hypothetical.* Suppose a negative change takes effect on 1 September on the Northbridge Open Formulary. Affected members are to be notified at least 90 days earlier, which means by 3 June. On the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary the same change needs 30 days, which means notice by 2 August.
